turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select
the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
SHG requires a non‑centrosymmetric lattice; magnitude is then boosted by heavy, highly polarizable anions (Te > Se > S > halides), d¹⁰ cations (Hg²⁺, Cd²⁺, Ag⁺, Cu⁺, Ga³⁺/In³⁺) and stereochemically active lone pairs (Tl⁺, Sb³⁺, As³⁺) whose distorted polyhedra add constructively in low‑symmetry (ideally polar/triclinic) cells.

Screening the pool:
- Centrosymmetric/high‑symmetry entries (cubic rocksalt‑/fluorite‑/spinel‑like such as c027, c037, c059, c065, c070, most SiC polytypes c024–c029, etc.) are rejected (d≈0).
- Sulfide‑only and hard‑cation frameworks (B‑S, P‑S, alkali halides, SiC, BeSe) are lower polarizability.
- The strongest motifs are Hg/Cd/In/Tl/Sb chalcogenides in clearly acentric, low‑symmetry cells:
  - c080 CsGa₅Hg₄Se₁₂: triclinic P1, Hg–Se (very soft, covalent), aligned GaSe₄/HgSeₙ units — classic giant‑SHG Hg selenide chemistry.
  - c073 CdIn₃Te₄As: near‑P1, Te (most polarizable), Cd/In d¹⁰ plus As lone pair.
  - c082 Al₄Hg₂Se₈: acentric tetragonal chalcopyrite‑type Hg–Se (HgGa₂Se₄‑like), large d.
  - c074 Tl₂Sb₂P₄Se₁₂: monoclinic acentric, Tl⁺/Sb³⁺ lone pairs with Se — strong acentric polarization.
  - c079 Ba₄Ge₂Te₅Se₃: triclinic P1, Te‑rich mixed Te/Se with Ge — very high polarizability, no inversion.

These outrank the good but more symmetric Ag/In/Ge‑Se chalcopyrites (c056/c071) and lone‑pair sulfides (c038).

Final: c080, c073, c082, c074, c079
